trust_decision.summary: The chain decides whether an asset's split-royalty percentages are valid (sum <= 100%) when an asset is created or its royalties are updated. It sums them in uint32 accumulators that wrap, so a split above 100% passes. The payout helpers in the accounts, ITO and market kapps then credit splitToPay without checking that it fits in the remaining royalty pool.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'integer overflow in split-royalty validation'. The uint32 sum and CheckValid100Params check in the asset-create handler are the obvious validation code.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once create/update cap every split field at <=100%, the ITO and market payout copies look unreachable with bad values. But assets that were already stored with wrapped percentages still reach them, and so do 100% splits that skip the debit.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Several splits that add up to exactly 100%, or one split at exactly 100% in every field, must still be accepted and pay out in full. The checks are gated by the FixMarketBuyOverflow fork flag so that replaying pre-fork blocks keeps legacy results. An over-broad fix (strict < 100%, rejecting when the remaining pool reaches 0, or an ungated check) breaks both.
